boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Rappahannock Station record (November 7, 1863) in the Bristoe Campaign [October-November 1863]. NPS describes the Kelly's Ford crossing the same day; whether the frozen record includes it is not established, and Rodes's Kelly's Ford losses are not added. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Corps; the live field reads zero. Humphreys says Russell's assaulting force numbered 2,117 and computes about 1,950 Confederates present in the works from Early's figures; he says Sedgwick called the defenders numerically equal to the attackers. Lee says a force estimated at three army corps deployed in front, and that the defenders, though inferior in numbers, could not be attacked on a wider front than their own.
claims.rationale: Assault-force, defender and army-level figures differ in scope; none is adopted. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Lee says the Federals had earlier built small earthworks on the hills, which his army converted into a tete-de-pont with rifle trenches, and that the works were slight but deemed adequate. Humphreys says a dam made a deep pool along the works, that Early criticised them, and that Wright called the place a strong natural position fortified with much labor. Lee says the valley and a strong wind concealed the night advance.
claims.rationale: Works in place before the day; their adequacy is disputed between Lee, Early (as relayed) and Wright. No map verification.

claims.value: Lee says his suggestions are the only explanation he can give and that the troops' courage is beyond question. Humphreys says Russell led the assault in person, that Sedgwick commended Russell, Upton and Ellmaker, and that Wright called it the war's first carrying of an important intrenched position at the first assault. The frozen commanders are General Lee and Major General Meade; the live heading ranks Lee Major General.
claims.rationale: Judgments are attributed; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 2,537 total (1,600 Confederate prisoners); the live field reads 2,502 (US 461; CS 2,041). Lee gives Early's loss, including the artillery, as 6 killed, 39 wounded and 1,629 missing, and Rodes's at Kelly's Ford as 5 killed, 59 wounded and 295 missing. Humphreys relays Early's figures as 6 killed, 35 wounded and 1,631 missing (1,672 total), and gives Russell's division 336 killed and wounded and 2 missing.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Kelly's Ford losses are a separate crossing and are not added; Lee's and Humphreys' readings of Early's figures differ slightly.

open_questions: Early's, Hays's, Russell's, Upton's and Sedgwick's reports and the returns remain deferred; whether the frozen record includes Kelly's Ford is not established.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Humphreys is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff in 1863–64, per his publisher's list. Stuart's, A. P. Hill's and Lee's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIX, Part 1, are separate families of interested Confederate commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
